prediction.likelyOutcome: GSL is very likely to win summary judgment on the core breach-of-contract/guaranty claims against both the tenant LLC and Nguyen personally, given the unopposed, well-documented itemized affidavit; recovery should land close to the $132,139.24 actually requested in the pending motion, plus continuing postjudgment interest. The main residual risk is that Nguyen's pro se lockout/conversion allegations get carved out for a trial on setoff rather than being summarily rejected, and that there is no support in this record for the larger 'remainder of term' acceleration figure the complaint originally referenced.

outcome.description: On September 4, 2025 the trial court granted the landlord summary judgment for $132,139.24, exactly the sum itemized in the landlord's affidavit ($104,295.80 overdue rent and fees, $3,000 clean-out costs, $12,416.92 prejudgment interest, $12,010.52 attorneys' fees and $416 court costs), plus 8 percent post-judgment interest and collection fees; the amount recorded here is the judgment less the $12,010.52 in attorneys' fees. The Twelfth District affirmed on July 27, 2026, holding the guarantor forfeited his lockout, notarization and phantom-LLC arguments by not opposing the motion.
